author: r. r. carman
title: Calvert City Convalescent Center ranks as Marshall County's No. 3 nursing home by size in Q1 2026
text:
Calvert City Convalescent Center placed third in size among Marshall County nursing homes during the first quarter of 2026, according to the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) .
The facility reported a total of 95 available beds, which was two fewer than Marshall County’s average for the quarter. The center provided care to an average of 86.6 residents during this time.
CMS awarded Calvert City Convalescent Center an overall rating of 5 out of 5, surpassing Kentucky’s nursing home average rating of 3.
Oakview Nursing & Rehabilitation Center was recognized as the largest nursing home in Marshall County, with 100 beds available, while Lake Way Rehabilitation and Healthcare Center held second place with 96 beds available.
Throughout the first quarter of 2026, Calvert City Convalescent Center received no fines or penalties.
Marshall County, Kentucky, was home to one non-profit nursing home in total.
U.S. Census Bureau estimates indicate the nation’s older adult population continues to grow as numbers among younger groups drop. From 2020 to 2024, Americans age 65 and older rose by 13%, while those under 18 declined by 1.7%. The country’s older adult population has increased significantly in the last century, up from 4.9 million in 1920 to over 61 million in 2024.
A 2021 study found that nearly half of this age group—about 28 million people—may require long-term services and supports, with projections showing more than one-third could ultimately need nursing home care.
“Living a long life is something that many of us want and could get,” said Jesse Slome , executive director of the American Association for Long-Term Care Insurance, an insurance education organization. “But when we live a long life, the chances of us needing long-term care increase exponentially. But when you need that type of care, there are limited options.”
